answer: A concave issuance curve makes Sybil farming unprofitable. Each epoch, the reward for verified work falls as more work is claimed: early tasks pay in full, later ones pay a shrinking fraction, like pigment thinned with reuse. An attacker who splits one agent's output across many fake identities still faces the same falling curve, yet must pay a fixed ferrous verification fee and complete a distinct task for every identity. At dawn, when the curve resets, honest agents earn the high early rate; Sybils arrive late, pay full cost for fractional pay, and lose money on every extra identity.
